title: Cliff as a solo pianist who disliked accompanying
summary: He wanted recognition as a soloist; he brought friends and Fat Cat into her Town Hall concert.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, you mentioned on tape last time that he was a little bit sensitive about accompanying a singer.
Because he wanted to be known as a soloist.

Yes, of course, I feel that when someone is recognized as a solo pianist they don't necessarily want to be accompanying, taking second fiddle to some singer, you know. But we did in '67, I believe it was, we did a concert at Town

Hall, I asked him to get musicians together and that's the one we got Tony Parenti, Max Kaminsky, Marshall Brown and Sonny Greer together and we did the concert.

I went down to -- Cliff was very familiar with Fat Cat -- by his being in these clubs, later after Cafe Society closed he was on 52nd Street again, he was at the old Ryan's on 52nd Street for a long time and then he worked at another club downtown, Lou Terrasi's (phonetic spelling), he was always solo piano and when Ryan's, the club, it had to fold because they tore down that area, Cliff opened in the new Ryan's on 54th Street so he was there for a long time.
So he had a lot of friends and a lot of people would come in to hear Cliff.
Do you remember any of the other musicians that he played with when he did play in a group context?
Well, you see, when he had the band it was before I came --
I mean in the 1950s, since you knew him.

didn't pay much attention to the musicians except when he was on 52nd Street at Ryan's there was the de Paris brothers, Sidney and Wilbur de Paris and he played at Lou Terrasi's, guys would come in there to work -- Vick Dickinson, Bobby Hackett, Slam Stewart and all the guys.
Then he played at Gondon's for a long time.
